purpose: Fosfomycin is an antibiotic used to treat uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTIs), especially bladder infections, in adults. It works against the bacteria most commonly responsible for these infections. It is particularly convenient because it is often given as just a single dose.
how_it_works: Fosfomycin works by blocking bacteria from building their protective outer wall, which they need to survive. Without this wall, the bacteria cannot grow or multiply and eventually die off. Think of it like pulling out the foundation of a building — the whole structure collapses.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, upset stomach, and headache. Some people may also notice a runny nose or back pain. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have any kidney problems before taking this medication. While rare, some people can have an allergic reaction — seek help right away if you notice rash, swelling, or trouble breathing. Also let your doctor know if your symptoms do not improve within 2 to 3 days after taking the dose, as you may need further evaluation.
typical_dosing: Fosfomycin usually comes as a powder packet that you mix with water and drink. For most uncomplicated bladder infections in adults, a single 3-gram dose is all that is needed. Your doctor may prescribe a different schedule if your situation requires it, so always follow their specific instructions.
